newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-INTER STAY IN HUNT FOR EUROPEAN CUP SPOT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER STAY IN HUNT FOR EUROPEAN CUP SPOT.

text.p: Internazionale recovered from losing the UEFA Cup final and English manager Roy Hodgson in less than a week to defeat Napoli 3-2 on Sunday and keep alive their faint hopes of a place in the European Cup.
But relief came only after England midfielder Paul Ince had threatened to add to Inter's woes with an own goal 31 minutes into the first half.
Ince made amends with a 50th minute equaliser before Chile's Ivan Zamorano and France's Youri Djorkaeff scored the goals that clinched a morale-boosting victory.
The three points keep Inter just two points behind second-placed Parma, who defeated Bologna with a goal from Enrico Chiesa.
With Juventus crowned champions on Friday, both clubs are competing for the runners-up spot that guarantees qualification to the new-look European Champions' League.
Lazio made sure of a UEFA Cup place with a 4-1 home win over relegated Verona, courtesy of two goals from Giuseppe Signori and one each from Igor Protti and Roberto Rambaudi.
Sampdoria and Udinese looked like claiming the two remaining UEFA berths after victories over relegation-threatened Cagliari and Piacenza respectively.
Perugia's third successive victory 2-0 against Roma lifted them out of the relegation zone.
